D3-AM to present new LAB II ceramic 3D printer at Formnext

, is presenting a new format of the LAB II printing system for technical ceramics at Formnext 2024. In addition to its Micro-Particle Jetting (MPJ) technology, the new system features a larger build platform, enabling new applications for large-format high-performance parts made of technical ceramics.

The LAB II large-format system from D3-AM features a build volume of 400 x 480 x 160 mm³ (L x W x H). This advancement is a direct response to upcoming customer requirements. The system enables the production of larger ceramic components or a higher quantity of smaller parts per print, thanks to the expanded build volume and the efficiency of Micro-Particle Jetting (MPJ) technology.

“The MPJ technology opens up completely new areas in additive manufacturing of technical ceramics,” said Stefan Waldner, Chief Product Officer at D3. He adds, “The in-house developed inkjet printhead technology is the key to processing abrasive and dark ceramic base materials. This is unique in the AM industry.”

In the MPJ process, water-based suspensions are used to form a green body drop by drop. After sintering, the manufactured parts can be reliably used even under extreme and demanding conditions, such as those found in aerospace and the semiconductor industry.

Anna-Katharina Hofer, Head of Material Development at D3, emphasized, “The continued use of water-based ceramic suspensions means that the debinding process is no longer an obstacle, further simplifying the production of ceramic components.”
